title: Finance Research Block Schema
description: Typed assistant-response schema for structured Block[] artifacts rendered by Chat, Analyze, and findings surfaces.

SubjectKind.description: Canonical subject discriminator. Ticker is a listing locator, not canonical identity.

SubjectRef.description: kind determines whether the id points to an issuer, instrument, listing, theme, macro topic, portfolio, or screen.

DataRef.description: Canonical backend binding for a block. Historical dataRef/queryRef language maps to data_ref in this schema.

BaseBlock.description: Shared render, audit, provenance, and snapshot binding fields for every block.

period.description: A result ref's period, as its financial answer labels it.

analyst_commentary.description: Analyst commentary written on a financial answer's results, shown apart from that answer.

comparison_gap.description: A scenario price comparison's decline or refusal (#224), so a later turn looks past it by this mark, not its words.

subject_labels.description: Display label per subject, in subject_refs order (e.g. a ticker).

series.description: Sealed series, one per subject and already normalized. When present, renderers draw exactly these and fetch nothing live.

subject_labels.description: Display label per subject, in subjects order (e.g. a ticker). Renderers fall back to the subject reference when a label is absent.

cells.description: Value matrix indexed [subjectIndex][metricIndex]. Optional: when absent the block renders metric labels with empty cells. A null entry is a gap (the subject lacks that metric) and renders as an em-dash.

primary_subject_ref.description: The queried subject to emphasize among the compared peers.

Sources.description: Provenance block required whenever external evidence appears in the answer.

Disclosure.description: Disclosure block for trust and compliance notes; orchestration may inject it.

FinancialPresentedPayload.description: Server-generated text only. A value's text is a formatted number; comparative words (highest, above, all) appear only in evaluated predicate or ranking results. An incomplete ranking labels no leader: an incomplete peer ranking names none, and an incomplete period ranking names the leader of the periods it ranked only in its text, with how many it ranked.

order.description: A peer ranking orders subjects; a period ranking orders one subject's periods.

FinancialTablePresentationV2.description: A v2 table: one column per line, so companies on different fiscal calendars share a column.

period_label_id.description: Null unless every row has a cell in this column and all read one period; each cell's result then names its own period.

FinancialPresentationV2.description: v1's presentation shapes, or a v2 table.

FinancialScenariosPresentationV3.description: P/E scenarios over one reported diluted EPS (#201): each row is that EPS times a P/E the user supplied. A mechanical scenario, not a price target.

rows.description: Exactly bear, base, and bull, in that order.

disclosure.const: A mechanical scenario: reported diluted EPS × a P/E you supplied. Not a price target, forecast, or recommendation.

FinancialPresentationV3.description: v2's presentation shapes, or P/E scenarios.

FinancialAnswerContentV3.description: v2 content whose presentations may include P/E scenarios (#201). Every other content stays v2.

FinancialAnswer.description: A certified quantitative answer. Every string is server-generated from committed results; there is no title or prose field, so a model cannot add unverified numerical or comparative claims.

financial.description: Generated by the snapshot verifier from the results it verified; callers cannot supply one. A version this schema does not know is accepted only so clients can show it as unsupported; it is never rendered as verified content.

ScenarioComparisonValue.description: A value as shown: its canonical decimal, the text shown, and the exact text for copy and accessible text.

ScenarioPriceComparisonContentV1.description: Generated by the server from a sealed P/E scenario's certified results and one stored close, and generated again by the seal; every string is server-written. It is source-linked evidence, never a verified calculation.

source_name.description: The source's stored name (sources.provider), shown for it; source_id and body_sha256 identify the record.

ScenarioPriceComparison.description: A sealed P/E scenario set against one stored closing price (#224): the price is source-linked, the differences are conditional on the user's P/E, and the block carries no verified calculation of its own.

CallFigure.description: A Call row's value as shown, or the named outcome shown instead of a number.

CallRow.description: One input of a Call, labelled with its kind (ADR 0005) and the basis it rests on; an agent assumption's basis says judgment or anchored.

CallContentV1.description: The agent's opinion on one company (ADR 0005, ADR 0006, #604), generated by the server from one certified run's inputs and the owner's settings, and generated again by the seal. It is never evidence and carries no verified calculation. Only a declined stance exists until an exit multiple can be anchored (#605).

Call.description: A Call block, headed "Agent opinion" and dated (ADR 0005): an opinion stored unchanged, with no verified badge.
